name: The Church
description: The Western Christian Church as a human institution in Mythic Europe, holding tremendous spiritual and temporal power and headed by the pope.

name: Greek Church
description: The Eastern Church centered in Constantinople and Jerusalem, holding sway only on the eastern peripheries of Mythic Europe.

name: Order of Hermes
description: The order of magi spread throughout Mythic Europe; troupes decide what the Church knows of it and whether it is seen as menace or ally.

name: Papal Curia
description: The papal court, where rumors of the Order of Hermes might circulate; its senior officials are recommended to have the Senior Clergy Virtue.

name: Cathedral Chapter
description: A legal corporation of the canons of a cathedral, very influential in diocesan governance and electing the bishop by secret ballot.

name: Knights Templar
description: Military order of the Church (the Poor Knights / Order of the Temple) given a full chapter in this book.

name: Franciscans
description: Order founded by Francis of Assisi, which faced difficulties before being accepted by the Church; also a Holy Tradition.

name: Poor Sisters
description: Franciscan order of women associated with Clare of Assisi.

name: Dominicans
description: Mendicant order discussed alongside the Franciscans.

name: Order of Cluny
description: Great Benedictine order (the Cluniacs) whose potential corruption is discussed.

name: Cistercians
description: Monastic order emphasizing solitude and manual labor, with a corrupt variant discussed.

name: Vallumbrosans
description: Monastic order of extreme asceticism and silence and total retreat from the world.

name: Joachimites
description: Followers of Joachim of Flora, connected to the Cistercians.

name: Hospitallers
description: Military order discussed among the other military orders.

name: Teutons
description: The Teutonic military order.

name: Order of Calatrava
description: Iberian military order.

name: Order of Saint Lazarus
description: Military order of the Church.

name: Order of Saint Thomas at Acre
description: Military order based at Acre.

name: Beguines
description: Holy women living religious lives outside formal convents; connected to hermits, with male equivalents called Beghards.

name: Beghards
description: Male equivalents of the Beguines.

name: Carmelite Nuns
description: Order of female religious discussed in the chapter on women.

name: Canonesses
description: Female religious living under a rule as canons.

name: Cathars
description: Heretics of Southern France targeted by the Albigensian Crusade.

name: House Ex Miscellanea
description: Hermetic House to which the sample Holy Maga belongs.

name: Guild of Saint Bartholomew
description: A guild dedicated to Saint Bartholomew, used as an example of guild processions earning Devotion.

name: Guild of Saint Peter
description: A guild dedicated to Saint Peter competing in the Easter Day procession.

name: Pope
description: The bishop of Rome and head of the Western Church, who crowns emperors and alone can create, divide, or suppress dioceses; has Commanding Aura with Magic Resistance 25.

name: Cardinal
description: Senior Church office; cardinals have Commanding Aura with Magic Resistance 20.

name: Archbishop
description: Senior cleric with jurisdiction over a province of dioceses; Commanding Aura grants Magic Resistance 10.

name: Bishop
description: Elected head of a diocese, chief priest, judge and ruler of his people, bearing ring and crosier.

name: Papal Legate
description: Representative of the pope, either legatus a latere or the lesser legatus missus, each with a Commanding Aura.

name: Archdeacon
description: Cleric governing an archdeaconry within a diocese.

name: Dean
description: Cleric governing a deanery within an archdeaconry.

name: Canon
description: Clergy serving a cathedral, forming the cathedral chapter that elects the bishop.

name: Priest
description: Ordained cleric in major orders who conducts Mass for his parish congregation.

name: Curate
description: Priest employed to discharge priestly duties in a parish on behalf of the benefice holder.

name: Chaplain
description: Priest serving a chapel, such as a covenant chapel.

name: Churchwarden
description: Lay officers who oversee and help run church buildings, developing in England and elsewhere.

name: Questor
description: Wandering preachers who sell indulgences.

name: Monk
description: Male religious living under a monastic rule.

name: Nun
description: Female religious living under a rule in a nunnery.

name: Friar
description: Mendicant religious; friar characters take the Mendicant Friar Virtue.

name: Abbot
description: Head of a monastery; a senior clergy position (abbess for women).

name: Hermit
description: One who renounces the world to live alone, celibate, observing the liturgical hours outside a formal monastic context.

name: Anchorite
description: The most extreme hermits, sealed into an anchorhold built against a church wall.

name: Mystic
description: Those dedicating their lives to pursuit of the love of God through contemplative or monistic mysticism.

name: Pilgrim
description: A traveler journeying to a holy site or shrine, facing ordeals on the road.

name: Holy Roman Emperor
description: Powerful lay ruler who may still attempt to appoint bishops, though such appointments are typically overturned.

name: Mythic Europe
description: The setting of Ars Magica, a patchwork of about 800 dioceses dominated by the Church.

name: Rome
description: Center of the Western Church and seat of the pope; a major pilgrimage destination.

name: Constantinople
description: One of the centers of the Greek Church.

name: Jerusalem
description: Holy city, center of the Greek Church and major pilgrimage destination.

name: Holy Land
description: Destination of major pilgrimages.

name: Santiago de Compostela
description: Site of the shrine and tomb of Saint James, a major pilgrimage destination.

name: Via Francigena
description: Pilgrimage route from Canterbury through France, across the Alps near Aosta, via Parma and Tuscany to Rome.

name: Via Carolingia
description: Pilgrimage route from Aachen through Strasbourg, Basle, Como, Mantua, Ravenna and Assisi to Rome.

name: Canterbury
description: English city at the start of the Via Francigena.

name: Aachen
description: City in northwest Germany where the Via Carolingia begins.

name: Assisi
description: Italian town on the Via Carolingia.

name: Ravenna
description: Italian city on the Via Carolingia.

name: Antioch
description: City on the pilgrim route to Jerusalem; Templars there are described.

name: Acre
description: Holy Land city with a Templar presence and the Order of Saint Thomas.

name: Damietta
description: Egyptian city where the Fifth Crusade is in 1220.

name: Bury Saint Edmunds
description: Town associated with Saint Edmund, where a white bull is led through the streets to invoke fertility.

name: The Alps
description: Mountains crossed by pilgrims traveling to Italy.

name: England
description: Realm with 21 dioceses, where churchwardens have developed.

name: France
description: Realm with 79 dioceses.

name: Italy
description: Region with almost 200 small dioceses.

name: Long Melford
description: Parish used as an example of petitioning the Church.

name: Fontevrault
description: Abbey discussed in the chapter on women, alongside Las Huelgas.

name: Las Huelgas
description: Abbey discussed alongside Fontevrault.

name: Anchorhold
description: A small bricked-up cell built against the outer wall of a church in which an anchorite lives.

name: God
description: Rules Mythic Europe in majesty, served by the angelic hosts; the object of Church worship.

name: Jesus Christ
description: The Son of God whose life and Passion contemplative mystics imitate.

name: Virgin Mary
description: The Blessed Virgin, Queen of Heaven, whom anyone may ask to intercede regardless of devotion.

name: Saint Bartholomew
description: Saint whose day is August 24th; example target of Devotion.

name: Saint Edmund
description: King and martyr whose day is November 20th, with a power to Bestow Fertility invoked at Bury Saint Edmunds.

name: Saint Jerome
description: Saint with a Power that pacifies wild beasts.

name: Saint Christopher
description: Patron of travelers; those who see his likeness and call on him are believed not to die that day on the road.

name: Saint Augustine
description: Saint and author of City of God, which counts as a hagiography for Devotion to him.

name: Saint James
description: Saint whose tomb and relics are at Santiago de Compostela.

name: Saint Peter
description: Saint to whom a guild is dedicated.

name: Francis of Assisi
description: Founder of the Franciscans; perhaps the only one to reconcile contemplative and monistic mysticism.

name: Clare of Assisi
description: Founder figure of the Poor Sisters.

name: Hildegard of Bingen
description: Female mystic and author discussed in the chapter on women.

name: Marie of Oignes
description: Beguine and mystic.

name: Elizabeth of Schönau
description: Female mystic and visionary author.

name: Héloïse
description: Historical woman discussed in an insert on female religious.

name: Christina of Markyate
description: Holy woman discussed in an insert on female religious.

name: Saint Severus of Ravenna
description: Saint discussed in an insert on women.

name: Joachim of Flora
description: Cistercian-connected figure whose followers are the Joachimites; associated with the Three Ages of the World.

name: Bernard of Clairvaux
description: Cistercian figure (1090-1153).

name: Father Tino of Gradara
description: Sample character in the chapter on corrupt orders.

name: Peter of Montaigu
description: Grand Master of the Knights Templar.

name: Elias Bonibarone
description: Minister-General of the Little Brothers (Franciscans).

name: Henri of Toulouse
description: Example petitioner in the Petitioning the Church rules.

name: Saint John of the Cross
description: Future systematic mystic whose works are not yet written in 1220.

name: Ignatius Loyola
description: Future systematic mystic whose works are not yet written in 1220.

name: Thomas the Shoemaker
description: Example devout character with Piety +2, devoted to the Blessed Virgin and Saint Bartholomew and owning a relic of Saint Edmund.

name: Boniface
description: Example werewolf character seeking removal of the Lycanthrope Flaw through a major pilgrimage.

name: Siderius
description: Faithful shield grog who pilgrimages hoping to gain Guardian Angel; True Friend to Boniface.

name: Chrétien the Roamer
description: Much-traveled monk seeking to lose Difficult Underlings who fails his pilgrimage by yielding to temptation.

name: Janus
description: Example magus who flies a ship to shore by a spell, overcoming an Oppositional Element alone.

name: Angel
description: Divine beings of the angelic hosts serving God; drawn to monistic mystics.

name: Demon
description: Infernal beings who oppose pilgrims, may carry souls to hell, and may be mistakenly venerated.

name: The Devil
description: Claims souls for eternal punishment in hell.

name: Ghost
description: Spirits of the dead that may rise if denied Christian burial or appear from purgatory.

name: Werewolf
description: A lycanthrope such as Boniface, a dangerous Supernatural Predator.

name: Faerie
description: Faerie beings, drawn to monistic mystics and possibly mistakenly venerated.

name: Elemental
description: Supernatural beings drawn to monistic mystics.

name: BaalBaruth
description: Demon, corrupter of monks.

name: Patarus
description: Demon described in the chapter on corruption.

name: Jaevert
description: Demon described in the chapter on corruption.

name: Varriar
description: Demon described in the chapter on corruption.

name: Divine
description: The realm of God; mysticism requires alignment with it and Divine Ascent affects characters aligned to it.

name: Infernal
description: The realm of demons, which may corrupt Church orders and mystics.

name: Faerie
description: One of the four realms; monistic mystics may come to see it as an aspect of God.

name: Magic
description: One of the four realms; monistic mystics may substitute Dominion Lore for Magic Lore.

name: Dominion
description: The Divine aura reflecting the real presence of God in churches.

name: Senior Clergy
description: Major Social Status Virtue for archbishops, bishops, abbots and other senior Church members, giving Reputation 4 and access to Church resources.

name: Priest (Virtue)
description: Minor Social Status Virtue for an ordained priest who can conduct Mass and is subject to canon law.

name: Clerk
description: Minor Social Status Virtue for an ordained member of the clergy in major or minor orders.

name: Religious
description: Minor Social Status Virtue for monks, nuns, beguines, anchorites, holy hermits and similar.

name: License of Absence
description: Major General Virtue giving a priest an extra free season each year.

name: Commanding Aura
description: Free Supernatural Virtue of Church office equivalent to Aura of Rightful Authority at Voice range, plus rank-based Magic Resistance and Soak.

name: True Faith
description: Major Virtue increasing Faith Point use; cannot be gained by Spiritual Path; higher scores grant Premonitions, double Magic Resistance and an Empyreal Aura.

name: Wealthy
description: Virtue representing personal wealth; wealthy priests are often pluralists.

name: Mendicant Friar
description: Social status Virtue to be taken by friar characters.

name: Temporal Influence
description: Virtue required for pope, cardinals and archbishops.

name: Guardian Angel
description: Major Virtue Siderius seeks through pilgrimage.

name: Unaging
description: Minor Virtue judged inappropriate to gain by pilgrimage.

name: Premonitions
description: Virtue gained at True Faith 2.

name: Second Sight
description: Always the first Revelation gained by a monistic mystic integrating Divine Ascent.

name: True Friend
description: Virtue representing a loyal friendship, as Siderius to Boniface.

name: Privileged Upbringing
description: Background Virtue not suitable for gaining by pilgrimage.

name: Educated
description: Background Virtue not suitable for gaining by pilgrimage.

name: Relic (Virtue)
description: Virtue representing possession of a relic, lost if gained through discovered simony.

name: Templar Prestige
description: New Templar Virtue.

name: Templar Confrere
description: New Templar Virtue for lay associates of the Templars.

name: Dark Secret
description: Major Story Flaw suited to a clergyman secretly violating canon law, e.g. False Presbyter, Heretic, Secret Wife/Husband or Simony.

name: Regular
description: Minor General Flaw: the character lives by a strict rule and must spend a free season on worship.

name: Monastic Vows
description: Major Story Flaw for characters who have taken monastic vows, to be used when the troupe wants stories about them.

name: Vow
description: Personality Flaw representing a religious vow; a mystic may gain it as a Quest Component.

name: Pious
description: Personality Flaw (Minor or Major) that counts as Piety 3 or 6 for establishing Devotions.

name: Difficult Underlings
description: Story Flaw where the character cannot control those beneath him, e.g. a priest unable to control his congregation.

name: Lycanthrope
description: Major Flaw that Boniface seeks to remove by pilgrimage.

name: Poor
description: Flaw representing poverty; a poor priest likely works as a curate or chaplain.

name: Visions
description: Flaw giving visions; monistic mysticism requires Visions or True Faith.

name: Twilight Prone
description: Hermetic Flaw compared to the monistic mystic's susceptibility to Divine Ascent.

name: Chaste
description: Personality Flaw suitable for characters affected by vows.

name: Dutybound
description: Personality Flaw suitable for characters affected by vows.

name: Higher Purpose
description: Personality Flaw suitable for characters affected by vows.

name: Lecherous
description: Personality Flaw indicating problems with a vow of chastity.

name: Avaricious
description: Personality Flaw indicating problems with a vow of poverty.

name: Church Lore
description: Knowledge of the Church; gained via worship and recommended for clergy.

name: Dominion Lore
description: Lore of the Divine realm; may hint at an appropriate saint and can substitute for other Realm Lores for monistic mystics.

name: Concentration
description: Ability central to monistic mysticism, determining experience from practicing Holy Abilities.

name: Civil and Canon Law
description: Recommended Ability for clergy.

name: Theology
description: Recommended Ability for clergy.

name: Artes Liberales
description: Recommended Ability for clergy.

name: Dead Language: Latin
description: Latin; recommended for clergy and required literacy for bishops.

name: Area Lore
description: Knowledge of regions, useful to pilgrims and improved by Care of Souls.

name: Leadership
description: Ability improved by Care of Souls.

name: Music
description: Ability that may be improved through worship.

name: Faerie Lore
description: Realm Lore for which Dominion Lore may be substituted by integrated monistic mystics.

name: Magic Lore
description: Realm Lore for which Dominion Lore may be substituted by integrated monistic mystics.

name: Sense Holy and Unholy
description: Supernatural Ability given as an example Holy Ability practiced by a monistic mystic.

name: Organization Lore: Knights Templar
description: New Ability covering knowledge of the Templars.

name: Devotion
description: Ability-like trait of focused veneration of a saint or the Virgin, advanced by Devotion Points and used as a bonus when invoking a saint.

name: Mentem
description: Hermetic Form; True Faith 3 grants double Magic Resistance against Mentem spells.

name: Aura of Rightful Authority
description: Hermetic spell to which the Commanding Aura power is equivalent.

name: City of God
description: Book by Saint Augustine of Quality 10, granting Devotion Points to those devoted to him.

name: Relic
description: Holy remains of a saint; gives +2 per Faith Point to Devotion Total and adds Magic Resistance.

name: Ring of Saint Bernard
description: Object of a story seed in the chapter on corruption.

name: Rule of Saint Benedict
description: The monastic rule governing Benedictine life.

name: Ancrene Riwle
description: The Anchoress' Rule.

name: Cum Delicti
description: Letter of approval for the Franciscans.

name: Indulgence
description: A certificate purchased with repentance and good works that mitigates the length of a decreed penance.

name: Purgatory
description: Place of purification for souls not good enough for heaven nor bad enough for hell; time there may be reduced by saints, prayers, Masses and perhaps indulgences.

name: Heaven
description: Eternal destination of saved souls.

name: Hell
description: Place of eternal punishment of souls claimed by the devil.

name: Limbo
description: Destination of unbaptized pagans.

name: Vigil
description: Night of prayer before an important event, costing a Fatigue level and granting a Confidence Point.

name: Fasting
description: Penitential abstinence lasting a season, giving +1 to Petitioning a Saint but a constant Fatigue level.

name: Devotion Points
description: Dedicated experience points used only to raise Devotions, gained through pilgrimage, endowments, guilds, miracles, etc.

name: Faith Points
description: Points spent like Confidence Points for +3 on a roll; they do not regenerate without True Faith.

name: Confidence Points
description: Points spent for roll bonuses; vigils grant one.

name: Invoking a Saint
description: Communication + Charm + Devotion Total roll vs 15 + die to have a saint use a Divine power on one's behalf.

name: Patron Saint
description: A saint a character may invoke for intercession, often of the local church, region or profession.

name: Sacramentals
description: Minor folk rituals and prayers, versions of invoking a saint.

name: Sacraments
description: Church rites such as Mass, communion, confession and last rites.

name: Mass
description: The central Church service; attendance and communion at least once a year is required.

name: Canonization
description: Formal Church recognition of a saint, requiring two genuine miracles and a cultus.

name: Dulia
description: Proper respect granted to an entity, which is not worship.

name: Latria
description: Worship reserved for God alone; offering it to others is a terrible sin.

name: Pilgrimage
description: Journey to a holy site; major and minor pilgrimages have Target Levels 30 and 18 and can grant Virtues or remove Flaws.

name: Oppositional Elements
description: Story obstacles of set values that each pilgrim must overcome, totaling the Pilgrimage Target Level.

name: Taking the Cross
description: Committing to a crusade in exchange for a free indulgence and a temporary Faith Point.

name: Albigensian Crusade
description: Crusade against the Cathars of Southern France, until 1229.

name: Fifth Crusade
description: Crusade that set off in 1217, at Damietta in 1220.

name: Fourth Crusade
description: Ill-fated crusade sixteen years before 1220.

name: Northern Crusade
description: Crusade against the Estonians, ending 1228.

name: Contemplative Mysticism
description: Mystical path of imitating Christ via theosis; its Divine Ascent takes the form of Divine Form and it progresses by Spiritual Paths.

name: Monistic Mysticism
description: Mystical path of losing the self in the oneness of God, requiring Visions or True Faith; its Divine Ascent takes the form of Divine Gloom.

name: Theosis
description: Process by which emulation of Christ lets the mystic participate more in the Divine.

name: Divine Ascent
description: Divine Warping experience analogous to Wizard's Twilight, triggered by gaining Warping Points.

name: Divine Form
description: Divine Ascent result for contemplatives, granting Soak, Penetration, Commanding Aura and punishment for sin.

name: Divine Gloom
description: Divine Ascent result for monistics, trading mundane knowledge for Dominion Lore and Holy Abilities.

name: Wizard's Twilight
description: Hermetic experience compared to Divine Ascent.

name: Warping
description: Warping Points and Score, which for Divine-aligned characters trigger Divine Ascent.

name: Spiritual Path
description: Series of Quest Components through which a contemplative mystic gains a Revelation.

name: Revelation
description: Virtue, Method, Power or Supernatural Ability gained through a Spiritual Path or monistic integration.

name: Quest Components
description: Valued deeds (pilgrimage, preaching, alms, crusade) totaling a Path Total.

name: Sins and Tempers
description: Classification of Personality Traits into sins (Proud, Wrathful...) and opposing tempers (Loyal, Calm...).

name: Celestial Disorientation
description: Effect monistic mystics resist more easily by adding Pious.

name: Empyreal Aura
description: Aura radiated to Voice range at True Faith 5.

name: Holy Tradition
description: Corporate Divine tradition with Methods and Powers; the Franciscans are one.

name: Methods and Powers
description: Holy supernatural abilities many mystics possess.

name: Holy Magic
description: Divine magical tradition one may self-initiate into via major pilgrimage with True Faith.

name: Magic Resistance
description: Resistance granted by True Faith, relics and Commanding Aura.

name: The Gift
description: Magical Gift possessed strangely by many monistic mystics.

name: Diocese
description: Ecclesiastical territory of a bishop; about 800 in Mythic Europe, grouped into provinces and split into archdeaconries and deaneries.

name: Parish
description: Basic unit beneath deaneries where a priest conducts Mass; virtually every covenant lies in one.

name: Benefice
description: Church office income; senior clergy may hold several and employ curates.

name: Canon Law
description: Church law to which clergy are subject.

name: Simony
description: Buying or selling spiritual things such as sacraments or offices.

name: Worship (Seasonal Activity)
description: Free-season activity of fasting, prayer and meditation with Source Quality equal to the church's Divine Aura.

name: Good Works
description: Seasonal activity of worthy deeds, Source Quality 2 and 1 Faith Point.

name: Care of Souls
description: Priest's seasonal activity of preaching giving willing congregants +1 to activities matching the sermon theme.

name: Tempering an Aura
description: Divine rule similar to Care of Souls.

name: Visitation
description: A bishop's tour of parishes questioning locals about their priest.

name: Third Lateran Council
description: 1179 council decreeing bishop candidates be at least thirty, legitimate and worthy.

name: Covenant
description: Home of magi; always located in or with an entrance in a parish.

name: Regio
description: Supernatural area; a covenant within one must have an entrance in a parish.

name: Heresy
description: Heretical interpretations of Church teaching, a danger for mystics and hermits.

name: Liturgical Hours
description: Daily offices observed by monks, hermits and some laity.
